front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
This Surah takes its name Al-Isra' (Night Journey) also known as Miraj is from Ayat 1.
The name (Bani Israel) from Ayat 4. But this name is merely a distinctive title like the names of many other Surahs and not a descriptive title. It is also called Al-Isra for the night journey of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The very first Ayat indicates that this Surah was revealed on the occasion of Mi`raj (Ascension). This event happened one year before Hijrah. Thus, this Surah was revealed in the last stage of Prophethood at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Background
front_matter.text: After twelve years of preaching Tauhid by the Holy Prophet, Islam had spread to every corner of Arabia. Now the time had come for the Holy Prophet to emigrate from Makkah to Al- Madinah so as to gather together all the scattered Muslims and establish a state based on the principles of Islam.

front_matter.label: Theme and Topics
front_matter.text:
The disbelievers of Makkah are being told to take a lesson from the miserable end of the Israelites and other nations and mend their ways. Incidentally, the Israelites, with whom Islam was going to come in direct contact in the near future at Al-Madinah have also been warned that they should learn a lesson from the chastisements that have already been inflicted on them.
The Islamic System of life or a sort Manifesto of the intended Islamic state in Madina is also discussed.
Tauhid is stressed, that is, the total and complete dependance/trust/reliance on Allah SWT alone and exclusively.
Additionally, the Quran has been mentioned in this Surah probably more times than any other Surah.

sections.title: ALLAH TOOK MUHAMMAD (PBUH) ON A TOUR OF THE UNIVERSE (1)

translation.text: Holy is He Who carried His servant by night from the Holy Mosque (in Makkah) to the farther Mosque (in Jerusalem) whose surroundings We have blessed that We might show him some of Our Signs. Indeed He alone is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

commentary.text: The Isra' (Night Journey)
The event referred to in this Ayat is known Miraj and Isra. According to authentic traditions, this took place a year before Hijrah.

In this Ayat, the Quran mentions only a part of the Prophets journey, i.e. from Masjid-i-Haram to the Temple at Jerusalem. The purpose of this journey, as stated here, was that Allah SWT willed to show His servant certain realties via some of His signs so as to increase conviction after bearing witness with his own eyes. 
One night the Angel Jibril took Prophet (PBUH) on al-Buraq from Masjid-i-Haram in Mecca to Masjid-i-Aqsa (the Temple in Jerusalem). There the Prophet (PBUH) offered his prayers along with the other Prophets. Then Angel Jibril took the Prophet (PBUH) towards the higher spheres. At last, he reached the Highest Place in the Heavens, and was received in audience by Allah SWT.

It was there that, besides other important instructions, the five daily Prayers were prescribed. Then he returned to the Temple and from there came back to Masjid-i-Haram. During this Journey, according to many traditions, Paradise and Hell were shown to the Prophet (PBUH).

sections.title: ALLAH FULFILLED THE PROPHECY MADE IN THE HOLY BOOK OF THE ISRAELITES THAT THEY WILL CREATE MISCHIEF IN THE LAND TWICE AND EACH TIME THEY WILL BE PUNISHED AND AL-QURAN GUIDES TO THE PERFECTLY STRAIGHT WAY (2-10)

translation.text: And We warned the Children of Israel in the Scripture, “You will certainly cause corruption in the land twice, and you will become extremely arrogant.

commentary.text: It was mentioned in the Torah that the Jews would spread Mischief twice

Allah SWT tells us that He made a declaration to the Children of Israel in the Torah that they would cause mischief on the earth twice, when after reaching the height of power they would become tyrants and extremely arrogant, shameless oppressors of people. Resulting in the wrath of Allah SWT.
To gain a better understanding of the history of the Jews pls read:
(i)  Dr Israr’s Book: The Rise and Fall of the Muslim Ummah.
(ii) Dr Israr’s Book:

translation.text: Surely this Quran guides to what is most upright, and gives good news to the believers—who do good—that they will have a mighty reward.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS
The Quran is a source of salvation and guide towards the right way or path leading to success (paradise).

sections.title: THE BOOK OF HIS OWN DEEDS SHALL BE GIVEN TO EACH INDIVIDUAL ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT (11-14)

translation.text: And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty.

commentary.text: When we make dua we should ask Allah SWT’s to decision what is best for us. Leave all matters to Allah SWT.

If we ask for something particular then we don’t know if it is ultimately in our favour. For example, maybe we are praying for marriage to a certain person, in our haste to get married, but in reality, it is going to be a disaster for us. So, we are actually asking for evil thinking we are asking for good.
Lesson: When making dua ask Allah SWT for the best in this world and the next. Meaning keep in more general as opposed to very specific in your request.

translation.text: ˹And it will be said,˺ “Read your record. You ˹alone˺ are sufficient this Day to take account of yourself.”

commentary.text: Our deeds and even our intentions will be displayed for us in multiple ways so that it becomes very clear to us where our ultimate destination is. We will not be able to dispute the decision due to its clarity.
Hadith: Whoever wants to be happy upon seeing the Book of deeds then fill it with excessive zikr of istikfar.
Also, good deeds erase bad deeds.

Dua for ISTAGHFAR is “Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi; Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilaihi”(Allah is free from imperfection, and I begin with praising Him. I beg forgiveness from Allah and I turn to Him in repentance.”
Read this 100 times a day for peace in this world and the next in sha Allah.

sections.title: HE THAT SEEKS GUIDANCE DOES SO TO HIS OWN GOOD AND HE WHO GOES ASTRAY DOES SO TO HIS OWN LOSS (15-17)

translation.text:
Whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good. And whoever chooses to stray, it is only to their own loss. No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another. And We would
never punish ˹a people˺ until We have sent a messenger ˹to warn them˺.

commentary.text: The Quran has placed great emphasis on the doctrine of personal responsibility. It means that, everyone is solely responsible for his conduct and is accountable to God as an individual. This doctrine has been emphasized over and over again so that a wise man should not act in imitation of another or justify his own conduct by similar deeds of others.

Thus, Allah SWT says if you adopt the right/correct t way then you benefit yourself first and foremost. On the other hand, if you deviate from the right way then you are harming yourself first and foremost.

sections.title: HE THAT DESIRES THE TRANSITORY THINGS OF THIS LIFE IS GIVEN HERE, BUT IN THE HEREAFTER HE SHALL BE CONDEMNED TO HELL (18-22)

arabic_lines: مَنۡ كَانَ يُرِيۡدُ الۡعَاجِلَةَ عَجَّلۡنَا لَهٗ فِيۡهَا مَا نَشَآءُ لِمَنۡ نُّرِيۡدُ ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا لَهٗ جَهَنَّمَ

translation.text: Whoever should desire the immediate - We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will [enter to] burn, censured and banished.

commentary.text: The Arabic word ‘ajilah’ الۡعَاجِلَةَ literally means something which can be had immediately. Here the Quran uses this term for “this world” or “worldly life”. It’s the opposite of “akhirat” (Hereafter) which the life of the next world after death.

The person who does not believe in the life of the Hereafter strives only for the successes and good things of this world. Consequently, such a person becomes a worshiper of this world and adopts wrong conduct, for he has no sense of personal responsibility and accountability to God and ultimately deserves the torment of Hell.

Thus, whoever desires this world then Allah SWT gives them this world although not necessarily what they are stiving for. They will receive what Allah SWT has decreed for them.  So, we find that worldly benefits are not guaranteed however Hell is a certainty.
Note: In the Quran this topic has been discussed before and after however here is the peak/core of the dialogue.
Lesson: Opt for delayed gratification and set your goals higher or greater results.

translation.text: But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it accordingly, and is a ˹true˺ believer, it is they whose striving will be appreciated.

commentary.text: Then in direct contrast to the previous Ayat, Allah SWT describes the outcome of those whose are focused on the Hereafter and strives for it -- with the necessary effort required -- thus seeking it in the right way, as a believer. Then such are the ones whose striving shall be appreciated, (rewarded by Allah SWT).

translation.text: We provide both the former and the latter from the bounty of your Lord. And the bounty of your Lord can never be withheld.

commentary.text: Allah SWT provides substance of this world to (i) those who strive for this world and to (ii) those who strive for the Hereafter. Allah SWT's favors are showered on all—the just and the unjust, the deserving and the undeserving. But there is a difference as explained in the two above Ayat’s. Note: No one else has the power to withhold and increase provisions.

Lesson: Allah SWT has given us all unique gifts and talents. Reflect on what we are seeking and what we are investing our time and energy in. Do not just strive for this world, children, career, etc. People fear that if we seek the Hereafter we will lose this world but indeed one simply gains and gains.

translation.text: Look how We have favored [in provision] some of them over others. But the Hereafter is greater in degrees [of difference] and greater in distinction.

commentary.text:
In this world some are rich and some are poor, and others are in between; some are beautiful, some are ugly and others are in between. In Paradise there are one hundred levels, and the distance between one level and another is like the distance between heaven and earth. 
The people of the highest levels (of Paradise) will see the people of `Illiyin’ Hell as if they are looking at distant stars on the horizon.
So, the division of the Hereafter will be much greater and eternal. Here there are differences but firstly it is for a finite time and secondly it is not as vast.

translation.text: Do not set up any other god with Allah lest you are rendered humiliated and helpless.

commentary.text: Do not associate Anything in the Worship of Allah SWT – DO NOT COMMIT SHIRK!
Shirk = Abandonment of Allah SWT.
Tauhid = Allah SWT’s help and closeness.

sections.title: SOME COMMANDMENTS OF ALLAH FOR THE BELIEVERS INCLUDING PROPER BEHAVIOR WITH PARENTS, RELATIVES, AND THE COMMUNITY AT LARGE (23-30)

intro.text: THE QURANIC VERSION OF THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

translation.text: For your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. And honour your parents. If one or both of them reach old age in your care, never say to them ˹even˺ ‘ugh,’ nor yell at them. Rather, address them respectfully.

commentary.text: The Command to Worship Allah Alone and to be (ii) Dutiful to One's Parents
In the following Ayat’s are some basic principles that form the manifesto for the new period at Al-Madinah where a new Islamic society were going to be established.

It prohibits the worship of anyone except Allah SWT. This was not merely an instruction confined to a religious doctrine and individual practice but it serves as the foundation for all ideological, moral, cultural economic and legal principles.
(Please also refer to Surah 6 Ayat 151-153)
The idea of worshipping Allah SWT is connected to the idea of honoring one's parents in many places in the Quran.
Doing good when parents become old is at times difficult but a Must. Also we must be good to both parents not just one.
Parents in old age:
Be careful of your language and tone. (Never hurt their feelings)
Do not scold or yell so that they feel intimated or scared of you. (God forbid)
Say words that are good, kind, and gentle.

translation.text: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small."

commentary.text: The metaphor is that of a high-flying bird which lowers her wings out of tenderness to her offspring. There is a double aptness. (1) When the parent was strong and the child was helpless, parental affection was showered on the child: now the child is strong, and the parent is helpless, so he must show similar tender care on the parent? (2) But more: he must approach the matter with gentle humility; all the while keeping in mind the other’s station.

Thus, not merely respect, but cherishing kindness, and humility to parents, are commanded: Parental love should be to us a type of divine love as nothing that we can do can ever really compensate for that which we have received. We cannot expect Allah SWT's forgiveness if we are rude or unkind to those who unselfishly brought us up.
Dua for parents: "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small."

translation.text: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.

commentary.text: The Command to maintain the Ties of Kinship, give to the poor and traveler and the Prohibition of Extravagance
When Allah SWT mentions honoring one's parents, He follows this with the command to treat one's relatives well and to maintain the ties of kinship.
And give to the Miskin (poor), and to the traveler. FYI -- All charity, kindness, and help are conditioned by our own resources.
And then there is a prohibition on spending lavishly and extravagantly so as to show off.
Lesson: Allah SWT gives us provisions as a loan to see how we use them that is are we giving in charity or are we mainly just indulging ourselves and family.
Additionally, showing off one’s wealth increases the rift and animosity between the haves and have nots.

translation.text: And if you [must] turn away from the needy awaiting mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word.

commentary.text: The above three instructions are meant to impress that a man should not reserve his earnings and his wealth exclusively for his own person. That he should also try and render the rights of his relatives, neighbors and other needy persons as well.

This attitude will help create the spirit of cooperation, generosity, sympathy and justice in the collective Islamic life. Thus, every relative will cooperate with the other and every rich person will help the needy in his neighborhood and a traveler would find himself an honorable guest among generous hosts. Thus, the responsivities and rights of human beings are interwoven.

However, if you have to "turn away" or refuse someone in need then do not speak harshly to them. Refuse with the sort of kindness (not merely frigid politeness) which flows from pity and understanding.
Lesson: If you cannot give financially then at least give them a kind/encouraging word.

translation.text: Do not be so tight-fisted, for you will be blameworthy; nor so open-handed, for you will end up in poverty.

commentary.text: Moderation in Spending
Allah SWT commands moderation in living. He condemns miserliness/stinginess and forbids extravagance.

translation.text: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.

commentary.text: Allah SWT gives and restricts.

sections.title: THE COMMANDMENTS CONTINUE (31-40)

translation.text: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.

commentary.text: Prohibition of killing Children

The people of the past were habitually committing female infanticide nor did they allow girls to inherit. Even today infanticide (esp female) is not uncommon in some countries due to economic constraints. This crime against children's lives (abortion) is one of the greatest of sins. 
 
‘And kill not your children for fear of poverty,’ means in case you fear their up brining and expenses will make you poor. This is why Allah SWT mentions the children's provision first, ‘We shall provide for them as well as for you.’
Killing or taking a life is a major sin including aborting an unborn child. FYI – Previous Ayat tells us not to be stingy.

translation.text: Do not go near adultery. It is truly a shameful deed and an evil way.

commentary.text: The Command to avoid Zina (Unlawful Sex) and Everything that leads to it
Allah SWT forbids His servants from even coming close to the sin of adultery or zina let alone commit zina. Keep at a safe distance.

Allah SWT calls zina or unlawful sex or sex outside a marriage as Fahishah (immoral sin) and ‘it is evil as a road (or a way)." Adultery is not only shameful in itself but it opens the road to many other evils. It destroys the basis of the family; it works against the interests of children born or to be born; it may cause hostilities, the loss of reputation, and also loosens permanently the bonds of society. Not only should it be avoided as a sin, but any approach or temptation should be avoided.
Lesson: Do not go near or put yourself in a position of temptation or compromise as one step leads to another.

translation.text: Nor take life - which Allah has made sacred - except for just cause. And if anyone is slain wrongfully, we have given his heir authority (to demand qisas or to forgive): but let him not exceed bounds in the matter of taking life; for he is helped (by the Law).

commentary.text: Prohibition of Unlawful Killing

Allah SWT forbids killing for no legitimate reason.
The blood of a Muslim is not permissible (to be shed) except in three cases: an adulterer who is married, and a person who leaves his religion and deserts the Jama'ah.
On the subject of Qisas see (2:178). Here under strict limitations a life may be taken for a life, or forgiveness is an option or blood money can be given.

translation.text: Do not come near the wealth of the orphan—unless intending to enhance it—until they attain maturity. Honour ˹your˺ pledges, for you will surely be accountable for them.

commentary.text: The Command to handle the Orphan's Wealth properly and honor or keep your pledges

When the Islamic state was established, legal and administrative methods were adopted to safeguard the rights of orphans. Then this principle was extended to cover the cases of all those citizens who were unable to safeguard their own rights. Thus, this is not merely a moral instruction.
If an orphan's property is handled at all, it should be only to improve it, or to give him something better than he had before.
‘Ashuddah,’ means the age when the orphan reaches his full maturity of strength and understanding.
Honor your pledges that is keep your word. Your word is your bond.

translation.text: Give in full when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is fairest and best in the end.

commentary.text: Command to be Honest in Weights and Measures
Honestly and fairness in dealings results in the blessings and barakh from Allah SWT in your riskh or provision. As opposed to having a lot ill begotten wealth that is nothing but ruin for you.
This instruction was not confined to individuals only but it was made one of the duties of the government to eradicate dishonesty in all commercial dealings and economic transactions.

translation.text: Do not follow that of which you have no knowledge. Surely the hearing, the sight, the heart - each of these shall be called to account.

commentary.text: Do not speak without Knowledge

Allah SWT forbids speaking without knowledge and only on the basis of suspicion, which is mere imagination and illusions.
According to a Hadith: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech.

The meanings of “Do not follow that of which you have no knowledge” is very comprehensive. Both in individual and collective life, one should not follow mere guess work and presumption instead of knowledge.
The Islamic moral code demands: Guard against suspicion and do not accuse any individual or group without proper investigation. In law, it is the concept of innocent before proven guilty.
In Islam we are encouraged to use inductive as opposed to deductive knowledge where we are urged to think, reflect, use our intellect. Stay clear of the occult science’s.

translation.text: And do not walk on the earth arrogantly. Surely you can neither crack the earth nor stretch to the height of the mountains.

commentary.text: Condemnation of strutting
Allah SWT forbids His servants to strut and walk in a boastful manner that is walk on the earth with conceit, arrogance and pride.

translation.text: The wickedness of each of that is hateful to your Lord.

commentary.text: That is, Allah SWT disapproves of anything that has been prohibited or, in other words, He disapproves of disobedience to any of these commandments.
Lesson: Allah SWT clearly summarizes/outlines what He likes and dislikes. It is up to us to put in the effort to understand and then change/adjust accordingly.

FYI – We meticulously keep in mind our children, spouse, friends, likes and dislikes then why are we not taking the time to recognize our Raab? Esp. when He as explained everything plainly and simply.
The beginning and the end of the commandments is with the concept of Tauhid.

sections.title: IF THERE WERE OTHER GODS BESIDES ALLAH, THEY WOULD HAVE TRIED TO DETHRONE HIM (41-44)

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Had there been other gods besides Him—as they claim—then they would have certainly sought a way to ˹challenge˺ the Lord of the Throne.”

commentary.text:
That is, (other gods) would have tried their best to become masters of the Throne. This is because if there had been more than one partners in Godhead, it would produce one of two results: (1) If they were all independent gods, it was not conceivable that they would agree and cooperate with one another in the management of the boundless universe and there could never be unanimity, uniformity and balanced proportion in its functioning. There would have been conflict at every step and everyone would have tried to dominate others in order to become its sole master. or (2) if one of them had been the supreme god and the others his obedient servants whom he had delegated some of his powers, then, according to the maxim “power corrupts”, they would never have been content with remaining obedient servants of the supreme god and would have conspired to become the supreme god themselves.

Whereas the fact is that in this universe not even a grain of wheat or a blade of grass can grow unless and until everything in the earth and the heavens cooperate with one another for its production. Thus, the very nature and functioning of this universe will serve as a testament that there is One and only One Sovereign ruling over this universe, and there is absolutely no likelihood of anyone else to be a partner in this at any stage.

sections.title: BELIEF IN THE HEREAFTER IS NECESSARY TO UNDERSTAND AL-QURAN AND HEREAFTER IS LIFE AFTER DEATH (45-52)

translation.text: When you ˹O Prophet˺ recite the Quran, We put a hidden barrier between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter.

and We place a covering on their hearts so that they do not comprehend it, and We cause a heaviness in their ears; and when you mention your Lord, the Only True Lord, in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion.

commentary.text: This Ayat is connected with the theme of tauhid.

If a man does not believe in the Hereafter, he will never consider the message of the Quran worth his while but will hanker after this world and its joys. Naturally his ears will not listen to the message and it will never reach the depths of his heart.

Allah SWT allows freedom of belief to practice shirk, atheism, disbelief with impunity and such practices do not appear to make any practical difference in this world. But, in fact, everyone shall be accountable and answerable after death in the next world.

sections.title: BELIEVERS SHOULD SPEAK ONLY GOOD WORDS (53-55)

translation.text: Tell My ˹believing˺ servants to say only what is best. Satan certainly seeks to sow discord among them. Satan is indeed a sworn enemy to humankind.

commentary.text: Reason: This was revealed about ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab. An Arab man insulted him, and so Allah SWT commanded him to pardon him. The idolaters were in the habit of harming, verbally and physically, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (PBUH). When they complained to the Messenger of Allah (PBUH), then Allah SWT revealed this Ayat.
People should speak Good Words with Politeness

Allah SWT commands His believing servants that they should address one another in their conversations and discussions with the best, most dignified and politest of words, for if they do not do that, Shaytan will spread discord among them, and words will lead to actions resulting in conflicts and fights.

sections.title: INVENTED GODS HAVE NO POWER TO RELIEVE YOU FROM ANY DISTRESS (56-57)

translation.text: Tell them: "Call upon those whom you fancy to be (your helpers) instead of Him! They have no power to remove any affliction from you, nor can they shift it (to any other)."

commentary.text: The gods of the Idolators can neither benefit nor harm

This warning helps to further explain the doctrine of Tauhid and negate shirk. According to this, shirk is not confined merely to falling prostrate before any other than Allah SWT but it is also shirk to pray to or invoke the help of any other than Allah SWT.

For praying to or calling for help any other than Allah is in reality a kind of worship. Therefore, the one who invokes for help any other than Allah SWT is as much guilty of shirk as the worshiper of an idol.
Simultaneously, this Ayat also shows that, none other than Allah SWT, has any power to listen to prayers and relieve our trouble/problems.
Lesson: Ask, pray to Allah SWT alone.

sections.title: WHY THE SIGNS ARE NOT SENT TO MUHAMMAD (PBUH) LIKE PRIOR PROPHETS (58-60)

translation.text: And We refrain from sending the signs, only because the men of former generations treated them as false: We sent the she-camel to the Thamud to open their eyes, but they treated her wrongfully: We only send the Signs by way of terror (and warning from evil).

commentary.text: Reason: The people of Mecca kept asking the Prophet (PBUH), to turn al-Safa hill into gold and remove the mountains [surrounding Mecca] for them so that they can engage in agriculture.
The Reason why Allah SWT did not send Signs or Miracles to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)

Past generations treated Allah SWT’s signs and miracles with contempt or rebellion, and thus brought about their own downfall. An example is cited from the story of Thamud. A perfect she-camel was sent a sign to this nation, however, the nation of Thamud continued to denied and killed her.  So instead of the she-camel being a reason for their salvation in fact the she-camel was a cause of their destruction – as now their sin and rebellion was irrefutable.

Signs, Miracles, and Prophets are sent by Allah SWT as a warning, so as to strike terror into the hearts of evildoers and reclaim them to the right path. However, it is Allah SWT’s sunnah that after a sign or miracle has been shown and if people still persist in disbelieve then the punishment is immediate and intense.

(Also see: 7:12)
He (Iblis) said: "Shall I prostrate myself to one whom You created from clay!"
Meaning I (Iblis) am better than he (Adam). You (Allah SWT) created me from fire, and You created him from clay. FYI – Iblis is a Jinn and not an angel.

Lesson: Allah SWT puts us through tests to expose our realities/faults. Iblis was jealous (in his heart) therefore his truth was shown.
By the end of our life our realities are exposed to all, whether we wish for it or not.

translation.text: Adding, “Do you see this one you honoured above me? If you delay my end until the Day of Judgment, I will certainly take hold of his descendants, except for a few.”

When Iblis asked for respite.

sections.title: NO COMPROMISE IS ALLOWED IN MATTERS OF ISLAMIC LAW AND PRINCIPLES (73-77)

translation.text: (O Muhammad), they had all but tempted you away from what We have revealed to you that you may invent something else in Our Name. Had you done so, they would have taken you as their trusted friend.

commentary.text: In order to understand the significance of this Ayat, we should keep in mind that the disbelievers of Makkah were exerting their utmost effort to turn the Prophet (PBUH) away from his message of Tauhid, and to force him to make a compromise with shirk and the customs of ignorance. In order to achieve this end, they tempted him with greed, threats, false propaganda against him, persecuted him via economic pressure and social boycott. In short, they did all that could be done to defeat his resolve.
They felt that the Quran was too rigid and uncompromising. They said change your religion just a little bit, touch our idols just a little bit and then we too will accept.
The Prophet was eager for peace.

translation.text: Had We not made you steadfast, you probably would have inclined to them a little,

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells us that in the matter of religion there can be NO COMPRIMISE! Not even the slightest change or inclination is acceptable. We have no right!
Allah SWT strengthen the Prophet (PBUH) resolve. The Messenger (PBUH) is given special strength to resist such temptations.

translation.text: Then [if you had], We would have made you taste double [punishment in] life and double [after] death. Then you would not find for yourself against Us a helper.

commentary.text: This implies two things: (1) No man, not even a Messenger of Allah SWT, can fight singlehanded against the deceitful methods of falsehood, unless he receives the succor and fortitude of Allah SWT. (2) If one compromises with falsehood after recognizing the truth, you might please some people but will incur the wrath of Allah SWT. For the Prophet of Allah, the punishment would be double due to his position.

sections.title: FIVE TIMES DAILY SALAH (PRAYERS) AND AND EXTRA PRAYER CALLED TAHAJJUD FOR THE HOLY PROPHET AND AL-QURAN IS A HEALING AND MERCY FOR THE BELIEVERS (78-84)

translation.text: Observe the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and the dawn prayer, for certainly the dawn prayer is witnessed ˹by angels˺.

commentary.text: The Command to offer the Five Prayers at their appointed Times

Perform the Salat from midday or when the sun crosses the meridian (when the sun begins to decline) until darkness of the night. This is understood to mean Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.  And recite the Quran in the early dawn meaning Salat Al-Fajr.
It has been ordained that the first prayer is to be offered before the sunrise and the remaining four after the declining of the sun till the darkness of the night.
The Meeting of the Angels at the Times of Fajr and Asr Prayers

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said that the Prophet stated that the recitation of the Quran in the early dawn is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.
The angels of the night and the angels of the day come amongst you in successive groups (in shifts). They meet at the morning prayer (Fajr) and at the Mid-afternoon prayer (Asr). Then one group ascends while the other stays.

Then their Lord asks the group that ascends to Him, although He knows best about you, “How did you leave My servants!”
They say, “We came to them when they were praying and we left them when they were praying.”

Though the angels witness each prayer and each good deed, the special mention of their being witnesses at the time of the recital of the Quran during the salatul-fajr gives it a particular importance. That is why the Prophet (PBUH) used to recite long passages from the Quran during the salatul-fajr.
The details of the timings of the prayers were reported in the Sunnah and deeds of the Prophet (PBUH).

Afterwards Angel Jibril was sent to the Prophet (PBUH) to define the limits of the timings of each prayer. The Prophet (PBUH) said: Jibril led me in the five prayers twice near the Kaabah. On the first day, he offered the Duhr prayer just after the declining of the sun, when the shadow of everything was the shortest. Then he offered the Asr prayer when the shadow of each thing was equal to its own length, then the Maghrib prayer at the time when one breaks hiss fast, and the Isha prayer was offered just at the time when twilight had disappeared, and Fajr prayer at the time when it becomes unlawful to eat and drink anything for the one who intends to observe a fast. The next day he offered the Dhuhr prayer at the time when the shadow of each thing became equal to its own length and the Asr prayer when the shadow had doubled. The Maghrib prayer was offered as on the previous day and the Isha prayer when one third of the night had passed away, and the Fajr prayer when light had spread all over. After this Jibril turned towards me and said: O Muhammad, these are the timings of salat of the Prophets and the right tunings are between these two extreme limits.

The Quran has also pointed to these five times of Salat on different occasions:

Surah 9 Verse Ayat 114
And listen; establish salat at the two ends of the day and in the early parts of the night

Surah 20 Ayat 130
And glorify your Lord with His praise before the sunrise (Fajr) and before sunset (Maghrib) and then glorify Him during the night (Isha) and then at the ends of the day (Dhuhr and Asr).

Surah 30 Verse Ayats 17-18
So glorify Allah when it is evening for you (Maghrib), and when it is morning (Fajr). Praise is only for Him in the heavens and the earth and glorify him in the later part of the afternoon (Asr) and in the afternoon (Dhuhr).

Forbidden prayer times are: 1- From dawn until the sun has risen to the height of a spear; 2- When it is directly overhead at noon until it has passed its zenith; and 3- From ‘Asr prayer until the sun has set completely.
There is great wisdom in this system of the timings of salat. One of these is to avoid the timings of the worship of the sun worshipers.

That is why Islam has ordained that the Muslims should offer their two prayers during the day time after the sun has declined and the Fajr prayer before the sunrise. The Prophet (PBUH) is reported to have replied to a question to this effect: Offer your morning prayer, but refrain from it when the sun is about to rise until it has risen high. For the sun rises between the horns of Satan and the unbelievers fall prostrate before it at that time.
Then after mentioning the Asr prayer, he said: After Asr prayer, refrain from any prayer until the sunset, for during that time the sun sets between the horns of Satan and the unbelievers fall prostrate before it.

The rising and the setting of the sun between the horns of Satan is symbolic expression that implies that both these times are used by Satan as temptations for the people. This is, as if to say: that Satan is so pleased with the worship of the unbelievers at the time of sunrise and sunset that he appears to carry the sun on his head as a mark of approval. This interpretation of the tradition is based on this remark of the Prophet (PBUH): The unbelievers fall prostrate before it.

translation.text: And rise from sleep during the night as well- this is an additional Prayer for you. Possibly your Lord will raise you to an honored position.

commentary.text: The Command to pray Tahajud
The literal meaning of tahajjud is to rise up by breaking sleep. Therefore, it means: Rise up from sleep after the passing of a part of night and then offer your prayer.
Nafl literally means: Something done in addition to an obligatory duty. This shows that the tahajjud prayer is in addition to the five prescribed prayers.
“Will raise you to an honored position..”means you may attain such a high position in this world and in the next world.
Ishraq or Duha Namaz (Same namaz)

The first half of the morning, from after sunrise (after about 15 mins), will be the time to pray Salaah al-Ishraq, and the second half of the morning until Istiwaa us Shams (zenith) will be the time to pray Salaah ad-Duha.

Lesson: Be in harmony and in sync with the universe. Wake up for fajr and use these best hours of the day. Worship Allah SWT as that is our fitra and that is why the universe was created. Conversely, initiating disharmony or chaos in this world is doing injustice or zulm in this world.
Remember we are all intertwined with each other so our vibrations of harmony or discord will resonate far and wide.

commentary.text: The Command to emigrate
The Prophet (PBUH) was commanded to emigrate from Mecca to Madina and then Allah SWT revealed this Ayat.
Prophet (PBUH) was told to make this dua before the hijra to Madina.  Then in Madina the Muslims finally found peace, security, financial and political success.

This dua is for going to a new place such as, a new house, a new country, a new job etc., and it basically asks Allah SWT to help bring about a good entrance and a good exit, that is, to make the change a positive one.
Man proposes and God disposes. That is, man makes plans; however, the outcome or result depends on Allah SWT’s support and assistance.
Lesson: Do not delay making this dua.

had it not been for the mercy of your Lord. Indeed, His favour upon you is immense.

Allah SWT has bestowed upon us many blessings and favors including, health, wealth, family etc. However, and by far Allah SWT’s greatest kindness upon us is the Quran. This is Allah SWT’s speech!
Lesson: Hold on tight to this Huge favour of Allah SWT upon us by giving the Quran is due that is, (i) recitation, (ii) understanding (iii) obeying and (iv) conveying. (2:121 haqqah tilawatihi)
The days I spend with the Quran are in fact, the best days of my life.

translation.text: And We had certainly given Moses nine evident signs, so ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, “Indeed I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic.”

commentary.text:
It should be noted that this is the third answer to the demand of the disbelievers of Mecca for signs or miracles. In answer to this demand, they are being warned: Nine clear signs, like the ones you are demanding, were shown one after the other to Pharaoh yet he did not want to believe in Musa (PBUH); then when he arrogantly rejected the Prophet, even after seeing the signs, Allah SWT drowned him.

The nine signs mentioned here have also been mentioned in Surah 7, Ayat 133. These were: (1) The staff which turned into a monster snake. (2) Moses’ bright hand which shone like the sun. (3) The public defeat of the sorcery of the magicians. (4) Universal famine. (5) Storm. (6) Locusts. (7) Lice. (8) Frogs. (9) Rain of blood.
