STORY OF PROPHET MUSA AND KHIZER (75-82)
STORY OF KING ZUL-QARNAIN (83-101)
FATE OF THE MUSHRIKIN AND THE BELIEVERS ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT (102-108)
WORDS OF ALLAH ARE COUNTLESS AND CANNOT BE RECORDED (109)
MUHAMMAD IS BUT A HUMAN BEING LIKE YOU (110)

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah takes its name from Ayat 9.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
This Surah was revealed in the third stage of Prophethood in Mecca which was from the 5th to the 10th year of Prophethood. What distinguishes this stage from the second and the fourth stages is this that during the second stage the Quraish mainly resorted to ridiculing, scoffing, threatening, tempting, raising objections and making false propaganda against the Holy Prophet and his followers in order to suppress the Islamic Movement.
But during the third stage they began intense persecution including a complete social and economic boycott. So much so that a large number of the Muslims had to emigrate from Arabia to Habash. However, in the tenth year of Prophethood and upon the death of Abu Talib and Hadrat Khadijah, the fourth stage began with such revere persecutions that forced the Holy Prophet and all his Companions to emigrate from Makkah.

items.text: This Surah was sent down in answer to three questions that had been put to the Holy Prophet in order to test him. These were: (I) Who were "the Sleepers of' the Cave" (II) What is the real story of Khidr and (III) What do you know about Zul- Qarnain.

These three questions and the stories involved the history of the Christians and the Jews, and were unknown in Hijaz. Thus, this was a test to see whether the Holy Prophet possessed any knowledge of the hidden and unseen things.

The story of the Sleepers of the Cave has also been used to warn the chiefs of Makkah who were persecuting the small newly formed Muslim Community. At the same time, the Holy Prophet has been instructed that he should in no case make a compromise with their persecutors nor should he consider them to be more important than his poor followers.

The story of Khidr and Musa conveys to us to have full faith in the wisdom of what is happening is with the will of Allah SWT. As the reality is hidden from us, we are often at a loss to understand the wisdom of what is happening, and sometimes (in our folly)  we question as to why?

The same is true of the story of Zul-Qarnain for it also admonishes the questioners, as if to say, "0 you vain chiefs of Makkah you should learn a lesson from Zul-Qarnain. Though he was a great ruler, a great conqueror and the owner of great resources, yet, he always surrendered to his Creator, whereas you are rebelling against Him even though you are insignificant chieftains in comparison with him.
Different stories are being related so as to provide motivation and guidance that Allah SWT’s help is the with those who believe.
What is Dajjal or the trial of Dajjal? And what is its relation or connection to this Surah.

front_matter.text:
Recitation of Surah Kalf on Friday will bring Nur for the rest of the week. Reciting even the first 10 and last 10 Ayats serves as a protection from Dajjal.
The root dajala means to mix. The word dajala is used to mean deliberately confusing matters and being vague and ambiguous, The Dajjal is the one who speaks in vagaries, who tells many lies and deceives many people.
The word “Dajjal” became a title given to the lying, one-eyed, false messiah. Any one claiming to be a Prophet after Prophet Muhammad is a dajjal.
The Dajjal will die at the hands of the Messiah ‘Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), as is indicated by the sahih ahadith.
In today’s world materialism is the Dajjal leaving them oblivious of the Hereafter and living for this world.

sections.title: THOSE WHO SAY ALLAH HAS BEGOTTEN A SON ARE UTTERING A MONSTROUS LIE (1-6)

arabic_lines: اَ لۡحَمۡدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِىۡۤ اَنۡزَلَ عَلٰى عَبۡدِهِ الۡكِتٰبَ وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَلْ لَّهٗ عِوَجًا

translation.text: Praise be to Allah Who has revealed to His servant the Book devoid of all crookedness;

commentary.text: The theme of the last Surah, that Allah SWT is worthy of all praise from His creatures, to whom He has granted a clear revelation, is continued in this Surah.
Surah Isar began with SA while this Surah begins with AH and ends with Allah ho Akbar.

The Quran is balanced and straightforward and there is nothing convoluted or complicated that would cause hesitation in the mind of a truth loving person. The Quran is free from error, falsehood or lies. It promotes a balanced way of life.
Lesson: The Quran changes one’s perspective and thinking whereby we are much more focused on the Hereafter.

translation.text: (He hath made it) Straight (and Clear) in order that He may warn (the godless) of a terrible Punishment from Him, and that He may give Glad Tidings to the Believers who work righteous deeds, that they shall have a goodly Reward,

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS

translation.text: And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."

commentary.text: The warning is especially for those who attribute a child to Allah SWT. Not only is this belief false but it invalidates everything as it is shirk. The root cause of Dajjal is this very concept that completely warps religion.
Lesson: We must inform others of this and not feel shy about it.

sections.title: STORY OF THE COMPANIONS OF THE CAVE (7-12)

translation.text: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.

commentary.text: This world's power, glory, wealth, position are but a fleeting show. Allah SWT uses it to test man to see whether he becomes a slave or seeker of this world (talib-e-dunya) or a slave or seeker of Allah SWT (talib-e-Akhirah).
Seek good company even force yourself if you have to. We will be tested throughout life and righteous company can be our source of salvation.

Lesson: The real test is to live in this life that is not cut off from this world and live in it as a believer. Live on this earth as if we are a guest meaning don’t get lost in it despite having much of the world in the palm of our hands.
This is the first sermon followed by the story of the people of the cave i.e. the nature of materialism and how we are not supposed to get locked up into the beauty of this world.

arabic_lines: اَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ اَنَّ اَصۡحٰبَ الۡـكَهۡفِ وَالرَّقِيۡمِۙ كَانُوۡا مِنۡ اٰيٰتِنَا عَجَبًا

translation.text: Do you think that the people of the Cave and the Inscription were one of Our wondrous signs?

commentary.text: Here begins the Story of the Cave (this was in response to the questions asked to test the Prophet).

The Quraysh sent a message to the Jewish rabbis in Al-Madinah to ask to test the Messenger of Allah SWT by asking him about these (i) young men, and about (ii) Dhul-Qarnayn (the man who traveled much) and (iii) about the Ruh.

This incident is not something amazing compared to Allah SWT’s power and ability, for example, the creation of the heavens and earth, the alternation of night and day and the subjugation of the sun, show that He is able to do whatever He wills.

translation.text: ˹Remember˺ when those youths took refuge in the cave, and said, “Our Lord! Grant us mercy from Yourself and guide us rightly through our ordeal.”

commentary.text: These (about 7) youths believed in tauhid so they left the city of shirk. They turned to Allah SWT for help.

It was said that when they called their king Decianus, to believe in Allah SWT, he refused and threatened them. The king gave them some time to think, hoping that they would return to their former religion.
During that time they managed to escape and flee from persecution for the sake of their religion. This was a way that Allah SWT showed kindness/mercy to them, that is, these young men were determined to flee from their people, and Allah decreed that for them.

translation.text: So We caused them to fall into a dead sleep in the cave for many years,

commentary.text: Allah SWT helped them. He made them fall into a deep sleep for many years and thus they received relief from their distress. This was a recompense for their actions. Meaning they did not just provide lip service but actually left their homes in the city of shrik and then asked Allah SWT for help.

sections.title: THEY WERE YOUNG MEN WHO DECLARED THE TRUTH ABOUT THE ONENESS OF ALLAH AND THEY HAD TO RUN AWAY AND TAKE REFUGE IN A CAVE (13-17)

translation.text: We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ their story in truth. They were youths who truly believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.

commentary.text: The Story of the People of Al-Kahf

The Arabic word Kahf literally means a vast cave. Now begins the essence of the story. 
The priority of these young men was deen. They turned to Allah SWT for help and guidance.
Lesson: Remember guidance comes when you desire and put in the effort. Guidance = desire + action.

translation.text: ˹Then they said to one another,˺ “These people of ours have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not produce a clear proof of them? Who then does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah?

commentary.text: Lesson: Fabricating a lie against Allah SWT by ascribing partners with Him is a huge mistake!

translation.text: Since you have distanced yourselves from them and what they worship besides Allah, take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will extend His mercy to you and accommodate you in your ordeal.”

commentary.text: As the youth had distanced themselves from shirk and worshiped non besides Allah SWT subsequently Allah SWT extended His mercy upon them and concealed them from the people.

Lesson: When you leave something for Allah SWT, for example, moving to an Islamic country, or making the afterlife a priority instead of this world, etc., then Allah SWT makes ease for you. But you must take the first step via some action with complete trust (tawaqul) in Allah SWT.

sections.title: THEY ARE IN A STATE OF SLEEP AND THEY WERE WAKEN UP BY ALLAH AFTER HUNDREDS OF YEAR (18-20)

translation.text: And you would think them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, while their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and been filled by them with terror.

commentary.text: Their Sleep in the Cave

Allah SWT had so arranged their refuge that none dared go inside the cave and if someone could have looked at the seven young men from outside and seen them turning from one side to the other at intervals, he would have thought that they were not asleep but awake. A fierce dog was keeping watch at the entrance.
This was the reason why their refuge remained a secret to the outer world for such a long period.
Note: The cave was big, comfortable, airy, facing the right direction from the sun (never giving direct sunlight).
In the Quran a dog is mentioned. It is ok to keep (i) Hunting dogs (ii) Guard dogs. Other than that, the general rule is that it is not permissible to keep dogs as pets.

translation.text: And so We awakened them so that they might question one another. One of them exclaimed, “How long have you remained ˹asleep˺?” Some replied, “Perhaps a day, or part of a day.” They said ˹to one another˺, “Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with these silver coins of yours to the city, and let him find which food is the purest, and then bring you provisions from it. Let him be ˹exceptionally˺ cautious, and do not let him give you away.

commentary.text: Their awakening and sending One of Themselves to buy Food

Allah SWT says just as He caused the young men to sleep, He then resurrected their bodies with their hair and skin intact with nothing distorted or lacking in their form and appearance. This was why after three hundred and nine years of sleep the young men asked each other, “How long have you remained ˹asleep˺?” Some replied, “Perhaps a day, or part of a day?’ They had entered the cave at the beginning of the day, and when they woke up it was towards the end of the day.

But they did not speculate much about this detail of how long they slept rather they turned their attention to more pressing matters, such as, their need for food and drink. So, with the Dirhams (silver coins) they brought from their homes, they sent one of the youths to buy Azka food. Azka means "purest" from the same root also comes the word Zakat, which makes one's wealth good and purifies it.
They tried to conceal him as much as possible so as not to attract attention towards him.
Lesson: Always eat good, pure, tayyab and halal food.

translation.text: For, indeed, if they find out about you, they will stone you ˹to death˺, or force you back into their faith, and then you will never succeed.”

commentary.text: They are referring to the followers of Decianus, who would punish them with all kinds of torture until they reverted back to their former religion, or they died. They knew that returning to their (old) religion meant they would never attain success in this world or the Hereafter.
Iman + Good deeds (action) = Success

sections.title: THEIR IDENTITY WAS DISCLOSED TO RESOLVE THE DISPUTED ISSUE OF LIFE AFTER DEATH, WHAT A SHAME THAT INSTEAD OF GETTING THE POINT PEOPLE ARE DISPUTING ABOUT THEIR NUMBERS (21-22)

translation.text: Some will say, “They were three, their dog was the fourth,” while others will say, “They were five, their dog was the sixth,” ˹only˺ guessing blindly. And others will say, “They were seven and their dog was the eighth.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “My Lord knows best their ˹exact˺ number. Only a few people know as well.” So do not argue about them except with sure knowledge, nor consult any of those ˹who debate˺ about them.

commentary.text: (Also see Ayat 26)

The controversy in later ages raged about the number of the Sleepers: were they three or five or seven? People speculated not from knowledge, but from conjecture. 
Allah SWT says there is no need to discuss matters without knowledge. If we are given knowledge of a matter, then we may talk about it, otherwise we should refrain. Remain silent.

Note: Most believe that they were seven sleepers and one dog. However, Allah SWT clearly is not happy with speculation and or innovation. We should understand and appreciate the actual lesson from the story and not get distracted with nonsense speculation.

sections.title: WHENEVER YOU PROMISE TO DO SOMETHING IN FUTURE, ALWAYS SAY, "INSHA ALLAH (IF ALLAH WILLS)"( 23-26)

translation.text: And never say about anything: "I shall certainly do this tomorrow"

arabic_lines: الَّاۤ اَنۡ يَّشَآءَ اللّٰهُوَاذۡكُرْ رَّبَّكَ اِذَا نَسِيۡتَ وَقُلۡ عَسٰٓى اَنۡ يَّهۡدِيَنِ رَبِّىۡ لِاَقۡرَبَ مِنۡ هٰذَا رَشَدًا

translation.text: without adding, “if Allah so wills!” But if you forget, then remember your Lord, and say, “I trust my Lord will guide me to what is more right than this.”

commentary.text: When the Prophet was asked about the story of the people of the Cave (as mentioned in the beginning of the Surah) he said, "I will tell you tomorrow,” but did not say in sha Allah. Then revelation from Allah SWT was delayed for many days.
Then Allah SWT shows His Messenger the correct etiquette when deciding to do something in the future; that is, always refer to the will of Allah SWT, as only He knows what was or is to happen.
So, when referring to something in the future always say:
“if Allah so wills!”  “in sha Allah” .  اَنۡ يَّشَآءَ اللّٰه
If one forgets to say it but remembers it later, even a year later, the Sunnah is that one should say it at that time meaning as soon as one remembers.
Lesson: This way we are leaving or transferring matters to Allah SWT. We don’t know if we will be able to fulfill our commitments only Allah SWT knows.

This is now become part of the manner or custom of our society that instills the concept of tauhid in everything we do and say. For example, we see a beautiful flower we say MA that is, we are not praising the flower but rather the Creator. After eating say AH to thank Allah SWT and so on.
Note: MA, AH and in sha Allah found in this Surah.

translation.text: They had remained in their cave for three hundred years, adding nine.

commentary.text: The young men slept in the cave for 309 years!

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah knows best how long they stayed. With Him ˹alone˺ is ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How perfectly He hears and sees! They have no guardian besides Him, and He shares His command with none.”

commentary.text: It is best to say, Allah knows best,” or ِ اللّٰهُ اَعۡلَمُ As only Allah SWT has all knowledge.

Lesson: Understand what is important in Islam via the stories in the Quran. Ask relevant and meaningful questions and not do not get caught up in nonsense of how many were in the cave or for example, people ask questions like, “how does one pray five times on the north pole as it is light outside 24 hours?”

sections.title: NO ONE IS AUTHORIZED TO CHANGE THE WORD OF ALLAH AND PROCLAIM, "TRUTH FROM ALLAH HAS COME, CHOICE IS YOURS, BELIEVE OR DISBELIEVE" (27-31)

translation.text: And patiently stick with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not let your eyes look beyond them, desiring the luxuries of this worldly life. And do not obey those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follow ˹only˺ their desires and whose state is ˹total˺ loss.

commentary.text: Definition of a Loser or Total Loss (Those who only follow their desires and get lost in this world)

Although these words have also been addressed to the Prophet (PBUH), they are really meant for the chiefs of the Quraish. The chiefs of the Quraish would say to the Prophet (PBUH) that they considered it below their dignity to sit with such underprivileged/poor people as Bilal, Suhaib, Ammar, Khabbab, Ibn-Masud and the like who generally remained in his company, and that if he can send them away, then they would be willing to attend his meetings in order to learn about his message.

Then Allah SWT revealed this Ayat. Keep yourself completely content with those who pray to their Lord morning and evening. Do not abandon these sincere but poor people so that the wealthy chiefs of the Quraish should come and sit near you.

This was meant to warn the chiefs of the Quraish that their wealth and pomp of which they were so proud has no value at all in the sight of Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH). In fact these poor people are more worthy as they are sincere and always remember Allah SWT.
Also see Surah 21 Ayat 31

The same was the attitude of the chiefs of Prophet Nuh’s (PBUH) people, who said: And we also see that none but the poorest and the shallowest of our people have become your followers. Upon this, Nuh (PBUH) replied: I am not going to drive away those who have believed in me.
Lesson: Not keeping good company will be one of the greatest regrets for people on the DoJ.

translation.text: And proclaim: "This is the Truth from your Lord. Now let him who will, believe; and let him who will, disbelieve. We have prepared a Fire for the wrong-doers whose billowing folds encompass them. If they ask for water, they will be served with a drink like dregs of oil that will scald their faces. How dreadful a drink, and how evil an abode!

commentary.text: Allah SWT says the truth is clear and the choice is ours. Meaning that any compromise or give and take in religion is not an option. Take it or leave it.
Punishment for the disbelievers is described.

translation.text: As for those who believe and do good, We certainly never deny the reward of those who are best in deeds.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS
Note: Good deeds should be done with the intention and sincerity of pleasing Allah SWT and the sunnah way.

translation.text: It is they who will have the Gardens of Eternity, with rivers flowing under their feet. There they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, and wear green garments of fine silk and rich brocade, reclining there on ˹canopied˺ couches. What a marvelous reward! And what a fabulous place to rest!

commentary.text: Here we find a detailed description of what we will find in Heaven in sha Allah.
Lesson: Opt for delayed gratification and opt for Iman and doing good deeds.

sections.title: PARABLE OF A BELIEVER AND A DISBELIEVER (32-44)

translation.text: Set forth to them the parable of two men: for one of them We provided two gardens of grape-vines and surrounded them with date palms; in between the two We placed corn-fields.

commentary.text: The main aspect in this story to understand is that shirk does not just refer to idol worship but also to the worship of materialism or money etc. This is the modern shirk – so to speak. People tend to place all faith and trust in material/money and forget Allah SWT. This is the shirk of our time as opposed to idol or sun worship. We are tested by our abundance and by the lack of it so understand the reality of wealth.
Also see Ayat 28

In order to understand the significance of this parable/example we should keep in mind Ayat 28 (above) in which the wealthily, arrogant chiefs of Makkah were told that the poor companions of the Prophet (PBUH) would not be cast-off/rejected so as to please or accommodate them.
The Example of the Rich Idolators and the Poor Muslims

Allah SWT then gives a parable/example of two men, one of whom Allah SWT gave two gardens of grapes, surrounded with palm trees and crops throughout. The trees and plants were abundantly fruitful, providing readily accessible, good quality produce every year without fail.
Lesson: We are being tested in this life with abundance as well as the lack of it.

translation.text: And he had other resources ˹as well˺. So he boasted to a ˹poor˺ companion of his, while conversing with him, “I am greater than you in wealth and superior in manpower.

commentary.text: The wealthy man puffed up with pride due to his possessions, his income, and his large family assuming that it would last forever. Looking down on his companion who was less affluent.

translation.text: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, "I do not think that this will perish - ever.

commentary.text: “And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself,” meaning, in his disbelief, rebellion, arrogance and denial of the Hereafter.

He said: "I do not think this will ever perish." Thus, he was allowing himself to be deceived by the abundance of plants, fruits, trees, and the rivers flowing through the different parts of his gardens. He thought that it could never come to an end or be destroyed.
This was due to a weakness of his faith in Allah SWT, and because he was so enamored by this world and its adornments, and because he disbelieved in the Hereafter.
Lesson: It was not wealth that ruined him rather his overwhelming and all-consuming love of the material. When we receive worldly blessings, we feel invincible. This is the greatest deception.
Don’t over-estimate the value of materials goods, Allah SWT can take it away any time.
So if you have nothing, don’t think you have nothing, you still have Allah SWT.
And if you have everything, don’t think you have everything, Allah can take all of that away unless you understand that you did not have anything to begin with.

translation.text: nor do I think the Hour will ˹ever˺ come. And if in fact I am returned to my Lord, I will definitely get a far better outcome than ˹all˺ this.”

commentary.text: That is, he said he did not think there is any life after death, but supposing there is then, he felt he shall fare even better in the Hereafter than in this world life, because his worldly prosperity is a clear proof that he is a favorite of God.

translation.text: His ˹believing˺ companion replied, while conversing with him, “Do you disbelieve in the One Who created you from dust, then ˹developed you˺ from a sperm-drop, then formed you into a man?

commentary.text: The Response of the Poor Believer
This shows that unbelief or kufr in Allah SWT is not confined to the denial of the existence of God, but also arrogance, pride, vanity and the denial of the Hereafter are also kufr.
In fact, belief in Allah SWT demands not merely declaring His existence but also the acknowledgment of His Sovereignty, Mastery, and Rule.
Three stages of man's creation: first dust, or clay, then a sperm drop and then when the different elements were mixed in due proportion, and the soul was breathed into him, this fashioned man.
Lesson: Reflect and understand our origin with is so base (dust, clay, clot of blood) as opposed to Allah SWT’s status and position. Never will we become arrogant ever again.

arabic_lines: وَلَوۡلَاۤ اِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ اللّٰهُ ۙ لَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ ۚ

translation.text: If only you had said, upon entering your property, ‘This is what Allah has willed! There is no power except with Allah!’ Even though you see me inferior to you in wealth and offspring,

commentary.text: Whoever is pleased with anything from his wealth or his children then say:
“That which Allah wills! There is no power but with Allah!"    َ مَا شَآءَ اللّٰهُ ۙ لَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ

Here the believer is telling the wealthy/arrogant man that, when he entered his garden and looked at it and liked it, why wouldn't he praise Allah SWT for the blessings of wealth and children that He has given to him and not to others! Why did he not say `That which Allah wills! There is no power but with Allah!"
Lesson: If someone is showing off then warn them or guide them.

translation.text: perhaps my Lord will grant me ˹something˺ better than your garden, and send down upon your garden a thunderbolt from the sky, turning it into a barren waste.

commentary.text: The poor man is confident that Allah SWT can provide him with much abundance whenever He wants and take away the wealth of the affluent man whenever He wants.

The specific punishment mentioned here was of thunderbolts and an earthquake is also implied, as it alters watercourses, diverts channels underground, throws up silt and sand, and covers large areas with ruin.

translation.text: And so all his produce was ˹totally˺ ruined, so he started to wring his hands for all he had spent on it, while it had collapsed on its trellises. He cried, “Alas! I wish I had never associated anyone with my Lord ˹in worship˺!”

commentary.text: The Evil Results of Kufr

"Fruits", "spent", "twisting of the hands", should all be understood in a wide metaphorical sense, as well as the literal sense. He had great income and possessions and through them he had great peace of mind and satisfaction, which now were all gone. He had invested a lot and trusted himself instead of Allah SWT.
Important to note there is no mention of any idol, deity, pir, or saint etc. Thus, the shirk mentioned here is the worship, reliance upon and complete trust upon materialism.

Maybe the poor persons feelings got hurt by what the wealthily man said. Never break or hurt the heart of anyone who is close to Allah SWT by unkind words or actions. Esp. words of pride or actions take due to a power position.
Haith: “Verily Allah said: ‘Whoever shows enmity to a pious worshiper of Mine, I declare war against him.
Lesson: The one who boasts about his power and possessions relying on creation, will be tested through them.

sections.title: SIMILITUDE OF WORLDLY LIFE AND ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH THE LIFE OF HEREAFTER (45-49)

translation.text: (Then he knew) that all power of protection rests with Allah, the True One. He is the best to reward, the best to determine the end of things.

commentary.text: Place your trust Allah SWT and not creation or yourself.  Allah SWT is our Wali. He is the best Provider and Planner.
Lesson: People have no control over their lives.  Wealth, family, children etc., all come to us from Allah SWT. So be grateful and trust Allah SWT.

translation.text: Wealth and children are the adornment of this worldly life, but the everlasting good deeds are far better with your Lord in reward and in hope.

commentary.text: Wealth and children are the adornment or beautification for the life of this world

Children and wealth are fleeting and useless worldly resources unless we spend our wealth in good things/charity and train our children to be righteous – then they will benefit us in this life and the next.

However, much better than wealth and children are good righteous deeds because they are our permanent asset and thus will be the reason for our entry into Heaven, in sha Allah. So, place all hope and expectations in your good deeds as opposed to your wealth and children. Good deeds will be our source of salvation.
Turning towards Allah SWT and worshipping Him is better than keeping busy accumulating wealth and pleasing our children.
Third time adornment is mentioned in this Surah as this is the central theme of this Ayat.

translation.text: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.

And patiently stick with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not let your eyes look beyond them, desiring the luxuries/adornment of this worldly life. And do not obey those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follow ˹only˺ their desires and whose state is ˹total˺ loss.

commentary.text: Hadith: The good righteous deeds that last are the five daily prayers. The good righteous deeds that last are the zikr of:
Subhan Allah (glory be to Allah)',
Al-Hamdu Lillah (praise be to Allah)',
La ilaha illallah (there is none worthy of worship except Allah)', and
Allahu Akbar (Allah is Most Great).'
Also see (3:14)
Beautified for men is the love of things they covet; women, children, vaulted hoards of gold...
Also see (64:15)
Your wealth and your children are only a trial, whereas Allah! With Him is a great reward (Paradise).

Lesson: Don’t cling to the world with all its sorrows and joys as it is fleeting and temporary. Make children an investment for you by teaching them well. We will be presented before Allah SWT naked, empty handed and alone just as we entered this world.
PLACE HOPE IN GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS

sections.title: FATE OF THOSE WHO FOLLOW THE SHAITAN AND COMMIT SHIRK (50-53)

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblîs, who was one of the jinn, but he rebelled against the command of his Lord. Would you then take him and his descendants as patrons instead of Me, although they are your enemy? What an evil alternative for the wrongdoers ˹to choose˺!

commentary.text: What a bad, miserable choice you have made by making satan your friend and guardian.
Mentioned here for the first time is the Iblis or satan was not an angel but a jinn.

translation.text: The wicked will see the Fire and realize that they are bound to fall into it, and will find no way to avoid it.

commentary.text: When the criminals shall see the Hell fire, they will realize that they cannot escape the inevitable. And in fact, this intense anxiety and distress due the anticipation and fear of Hell is in itself a real punishment.

sections.title: ALLAH HAS GIVEN ALL KINDS OF EXAMPLES IN THE QURAN, SO THAT THE PEOPLE MAY UNDERSTAND HIS MESSAGE (54-59)

translation.text: We have explained in detail in this Quran, for the benefit of mankind, every kind of similitude: but man is, in most things, contentious.

commentary.text: Also see Surah Bani Israel Ayat 89
Examples put forth in the Quran
In the Quran, Allah SWT has explained matters with examples and in different ways, so that the path of guidance is clear. Yet, man is very argumentative and in the habit of debate and stubbornness.
Lesson: When Iman enters one’s heart, he comes less argumentative and more accepting.

translation.text: And who does more wrong than those who, when reminded of their Lord’s revelations, turn away from them and forget what their own hands have done? We have certainly cast veils over their hearts—leaving them unable to comprehend this ˹Quran˺—and deafness in their ears. And if you ˹O Prophet˺ invite them to ˹true˺ guidance, they will never be ˹rightly˺ guided.

commentary.text: Also see Surah Bani Israel Ayat 36
The Worst People are Those Who turn away after being reminded
Allah SWT says the worst among mankind are those who after being reminded choose to ignore, not listen or pay attention to the Quran and its teachings.

“Forget what their own hands have done,” meaning they forget their wrong actions and bad deeds. That is, if they are adopted Iman and repented in this world then they could have achieved total salvation. Instaed they choose to ignore and turn away for the Quran and its teachings.
Then for such people Allah SWT has set a seal or coverings over their hearts so that they will not understand this Quran and its clear Message. They will be deaf in an abstract way, to guidance.
This is the fate of those who adopt the attitude of contention, dispute, wrangling and argument towards the caution of a well-wisher.

Lesson: This is the most awful fate and worst punishment. The gift of guidance is removed. Remember it is but natural for a human to sin so do not fear sin as we can seek/beg for repentance but DO fear when the Quran leaves one’s heart.

sections.title: PROPHET MUSA TRAVELLED TO FIND KHIZER TO LEARN SOME OF THE KNOWLEDGE GIVEN TO HIM BY ALLAH ALMIGHTY AND KHIZER WARNED MUSA THAT HE WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO BEAR WITH HIM (60-70)

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when Moses said to his young assistant, “I will never give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if I travel for ages.”

commentary.text: The theme of crux of this story is that in this world although we may find something apparently bad or objectionable we do not understand the wisdom of Allah SWT behind this apparent wrong. So one should just leave things and the decree to the will of Allah SWT. Allah SWT decrees only khair or good for us but in our short-sightedness, we cannot see that. A Momin is happy with Allah’s rulings whatever it may be. Always continue to seek knowledge and do not get arrogant about the knowledge that Allah SWT has bestowed upon you as it is one of Allah SWT’s greatest blessings. Have sabr/patience.
Surah Al-Bakarah Ayat 216

Fighting has been made obligatory upon you ˹believers˺, though you dislike it. Perhaps you dislike something which is good for you and like something which is bad for you. Allah knows and you do not know.
The Story of Musa and Al-Khidr
Musa was commanded by Allah SWT to travel to one of his servants who had knowledge which Musa had not been granted. This servant of Allah SWT was situated at the junction of the two seas.

translation.text: But when they ˹finally˺ reached the point where the seas met, they forgot their ˹salted˺ fish, and it made its way into the sea, slipping away ˹wondrously˺.

commentary.text:
Musa had been commanded to carry a salted fish with him, and it had been said to him that when you lose the fish, that will be a sign that you have reached the right place. So, they set out and traveled until they reached the junction of the two seas.

The dead fish came back to life and jumped into the sea creating a tunnel as it swam away. Both Musa and Yusha` were asleep however when the fish jumped out of the boat Yusha woke up and saw it swim away however he did not tell Musa about this.

translation.text: When they had passed further, he said to his assistant, “Bring us our meal! We have certainly been exhausted by today’s journey.”

commentary.text: Musa forgot about the fish, and his attendant forgot to tell him of the fact that he had seen the fish escaping into the sea. Thus, we find that it was a blessing from Allah SWT to make Musa tired and hungry because only then did he realize that the fish was missing.
Lesson: At times illness, exhaustion etc., are a mercy from Allah SWT that we regroup and take a break.

translation.text: He replied, “Do you remember when we rested by the rock? ˹That is when˺ I forgot the fish. None made me forget to mention this except Satan. And the fish made its way into the sea miraculously.”

commentary.text: The servant truthfully confessed everything to Musa about the fish that is, how is swam away into the ocean.

translation.text: Moses responded, “That is ˹exactly˺ what we were looking for.” So they returned, retracing their footsteps.

commentary.text: Musa then retraced his steps.

Lesson: Musa did not yell, insult or blame his servant. When we set goals then we are tested in many ways so as to assess our level of commitment. Being tolerant when others make a mistake is real sabr/patience.

translation.text: There they found a servant of Ours, to whom We had granted mercy from Us and enlightened with knowledge of Our Own.

commentary.text: This righteous servant was given special knowledge and mercy from Allah SWT.

translation.text: Moses said to him, “May I follow you, provided that you teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?”

commentary.text: Musa meeting with Al-Khidr and accompanying Him
Musa asked if he could accompany Khidr and learn from him so that he may be guided and do righteous deeds.

translation.text: He said, “You certainly cannot be patient ˹enough˺ with me.

commentary.text: Meaning that when Musa will see Khidr doing things that go against his law then Musa will not be able to restrain himself.

translation.text: And how can you be patient with what is beyond your ˹realm of˺ knowledge?”

commentary.text: Al-Khir knew that Musa will criticize or even condemn him however, Al-Khir had knowledge of Allah's wisdom and the hidden interests which only he could see.

arabic_lines: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىۡۤ اِنۡ شَآءَ اللّٰهُ صَابِرًا وَّلَاۤ اَعۡصِىۡ لَكَ اَمۡرًا

translation.text: Moses assured ˹him˺, “You will find me patient, Allah willing, and I will not disobey any of your orders.”

commentary.text: Musa adopts the correct attitude of the learner to the Teacher, and promises to obey all things, with the help of Allah SWT. The Teacher is doubtful but permits him to follow him on condition that he asks no questions about anything until the Teacher himself mentions it first.

translation.text: He responded, “Then if you follow me, do not question me about anything until I ˹myself˺ clarify it for you.”

commentary.text: Al-Khidr sets one condition that do not ask me about anything till I tell you. Just observe and do not comment. Questions will be allowed till at the end so do not interpret before.

sections.title: PROPHET MUSA COULD NOT RESIST QUESTIONING KHIZER WHEN HE MADE A HOLE IN BOAT, AND WHEN HE KILLED A BOY WITH NO APPARENT REASON (71-74)

translation.text: So they set out, but after they had boarded a ship, the man made a hole in it. Moses protested, “Have you done this to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing!”

commentary.text: Damaging the Boat

Al-Khidr had made the condition that Musa should not ask him about anything he found objectionable until he (Al-Khidr) himself initiated the discussion and offered an explanation. Allah SWT tells us that after having come to an agreement and reached an understanding, Musa and Al-Khidr set out.

So, they went on board the ship. When the boat took was out to sea and they were far from the shore, Al-Khidr got up and damaged the boat, pulling out one of its planks.  Musa, could not restrain himself from being critical.

translation.text: [Al-Khidh r] said, "Did I not say that with me you would never be able to have patience?"

commentary.text: Al-Khidr reminded Musa of their previously agreed terms/condition, that was, ‘do not denounce me because you do not know the full story, and there is a reason and purpose for what I do.’

translation.text: Moses pleaded, “Excuse me for forgetting, and do not be hard on me.”

commentary.text: Musa immediately apologized and asked for pardon/leniency. He was not argumentative and suborn.

translation.text: So they proceeded until they came across a boy, and the man killed him. Moses protested, “Have you killed an innocent soul, who killed no one? You have certainly done a horrible thing.”

commentary.text: The Story of killing the Boy

They continued after the first incident, till they met a boy, and he (Al Khidr) killed him.
It has been stated previously that this boy was playing with other boys in one of the towns, and that Al-Khidr deliberately singled him out. He was the finest and most handsome of them all, and Al-Khidr killed him. When Musa, saw that he denounced him even more fervently than in the first case, and said hastily: ‘Have you killed an innocent person?’ meaning, a young person who had not yet committed any sin or done anything wrong.
Note: Until a child reaches puberty his sins are not recorded. Only good deeds are recorded.
Musa again apologized to Al-Khidr for his interruption and asked for pardon one last time.
